records.title: Authoring trail is now append-only, boot-gated and exportable per document; the signature stores are still missing from the boot gate, the per-document export and the signature register
records.evidenceAtHead: CLOSED: (1) db/migrations/20260725_authoring_audit_trail.sql:72-110 now creates trg_authoring_audit_trail_append_only / _no_truncate (amended in place, 7863cf830), and both are required by the boot gate and the daily sweep at server/services/audit/audit-immutability-triggers.ts:60-61. (2) Actor: server/services/authoring/authoring-evidence.ts:170-176 passes ctx.actorId (at 92ccdba1 it passed ctx.actorEmail, which Number() turned into NULL). (3) A transactional authoring write now chains into audit_logs on the caller's client, with trailId and metadataSha256 (authoring-evidence.ts:178-200). (4) GET /api/authoring/docs/:docId/audit/export (server/routes/authoring.router.ts:7703-7785) is a per-document record export: it is recorded on the chain before anything is sent, and it is wired into the client (client/src/concept2cure/v2/editor/DocumentWorkbench.tsx:2515). (5) authoring_signatures is append-only by trigger (migrations/20261001_domain_history_append_only.sql:174-178, on the C2C set at scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:2883) and under the runtime-role ceiling (scripts/db/provision-app-role.mjs APPEND_ONLY list). (6) The runtime role holds only SELECT and INSERT on ai.gateway_audit_log (db/migrations/20260813_ai_gateway_audit_log.sql:252; provision-app-role.mjs:229). OPEN: (a) EXPECTED_AUDIT_IMMUTABILITY_TRIGGERS (audit-immutability-triggers.ts:44-88) does not list the authoring_signatures triggers, nor workflow_history, document_audit_logs, regulatory_audit_logs or c2c_ana_actions. server/db/__tests__/provision-app-role-append-only.test.ts:156 says 'the boot does not require that trigger yet'. (b) ai.gateway_audit_log still has no trigger; the migration header declines one on purpose, so the owner role can still UPDATE or DELETE rows. (c) The per-document export loads only authoring_audit_trail plus chained rows matching action LIKE 'authoring.section.%' that carry details.trailId (server/services/authoring/authoring-record.ts:261-290). The sign, freeze and e-sign handlers write their chained rows as 'authoring.document.sign' (authoring.router.ts:7516-7524), 'authoring.document.freeze' (:5183-5194) and 'authoring.document.e-sign' (~:5431), all without a trailId. Their trail rows are therefore exported with no chain entry (intact null), and no authoring_signatures row is included at all. The export is JSON only and capped at 10,000 rows, with a truncated flag. (d) The org-wide signed export still reads only audit_events (server/services/audit/signedAuditExport.ts:280, :474) and audit_logs (:406), with a 50,000-row cap (:382). (e) The electronic signature register report (server/services/audit/compliance-reports/queries/electronic-signatures.ts:51) reads only electronic_signatures. Authoring signatures go only into authoring_signatures (authoring.router.ts:4920, 7448; note at :5340-5346), so they are absent from the register, and the report's notRecorded list (:107-109) does not say so. (f) server/services/audit/domain-history-link.ts:167-171 still marks authoring_audit_trail linked:false (stale).
records.fixedBy: 7863cf830 (authoring_audit_trail triggers, db/migrations/20260725_authoring_audit_trail.sql:72-110; boot-gate entries in audit-immutability-triggers.ts:60-61; per-document export at authoring.router.ts:7703); 0265be3cd (actor id in authoring-evidence.ts:170-176); 00f94ee9f (authoring_signatures append-only trigger, migrations/20261001_domain_history_append_only.sql:174-178); fd69c098d (ai.gateway_audit_log and authoring_signatures under the SELECT/INSERT grant ceiling)
records.remaining: (1) The boot gate and daily sweep do not require the authoring_signatures triggers or the other four domain-history triggers. A disabled trigger goes undetected. (2) The per-document record export leaves out the signatures (authoring_signatures) and cannot verify the SIGN, FREEZE and E-SIGN events: their chained rows carry no trailId and use an action the loader filters out. (3) The electronic signature register report leaves out Authoring signatures (authoring_signatures) and artifact signatures (concept2cure_signatures), and does not say so. (4) ai.gateway_audit_log has no trigger, only a grant ceiling. (5) The org-wide signed export covers only audit_logs and audit_events (authoring events appear only as their chained index rows) and is capped at 50,000 rows. (6) The domain-history-link registry entry is stale. (7) There is no human-readable (PDF) record export.
records.severityRationale: The core of the original P1 is closed. The authoritative authoring trail is DB-immutable and boot-gated. Every transactional authoring act chains into audit_logs with a non-null actor. An inspector can pull a recorded, verifiable per-document export. Signature rows are DB-immutable, are shown on the document, and appear as chained audit_logs rows in the org-wide signed export. What remains is completeness and boot-gate coverage of signature stores in aggregate reports and exports: an enterprise-GA audit finding, not a reason a founder-supported pilot cannot rely on the records.
records.humanTestingNote: Sign, freeze or e-sign a document in Authoring, then run Reporting & analytics > Audit & compliance reports > Electronic signature register. The Authoring signatures are not listed, and the report does not say they are excluded. In the document's 'Export record' JSON, the SIGN/FREEZE/E-SIGN events have no chain entry (integrity intact = null) and there is no signatures section. Workaround: read the signatures on the document's Signatures panel (GET /api/authoring/docs/:docId/signatures) or in the org-wide signed audit export, which carries the authoring.document.sign/freeze/e-sign chained rows.

records.title: Member role change and removal are now audited in-transaction with reason and old/new role; platform suspension and membership grants are still not on the tenant's chain
records.evidenceAtHead: CLOSED: (1) PATCH /api/tenant-users/:organizationId/:userId (server/routes/tenant-users.ts:575-636) and DELETE (:643-692) require a reason: memberChangeReason, otherwise 400 REASON_REQUIRED (:49-58). They lock the admin rows and run changeMemberRole / removeMember inside one transaction (server/services/tenant/membership-change.ts:81-101, 143-158). Each writes writeChainedAuditRow on the caller's client with previousRole, newRole, reason, actor, IP and user agent (:49-67) before COMMIT, and a refused audit row rolls the change back. (2) The membership cache is invalidated after commit (tenant-users.ts:627, :685). (3) SCIM removal is audited in its transaction (server/routes/scim.ts:416-440). (4) The client sends the reason (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/AdminMemberActions.tsx:175). Ran `npx vitest run server/routes/__tests__/tenant-users-audit.test.ts`: 25/25 pass, including 'a failed audit write rolls the change back' and 'writes one chained row on the removal transaction, before COMMIT'. OPEN: (a) Platform suspend/reactivate (server/routes/admin/master-admin.ts:408-460) still commits UPDATE users, then calls recordAuditRow with tenantId 0 on a separate connection, best-effort. The organisation's chain and export never show it. (b) There is no tenant-level suspend: organization_users has no status column (shared/schema.ts:2641-2660), and no suspend route exists under /api/tenant-users. (c) Membership grants are not on the chain. atomicCreateUser (server/services/atomicQuotaService.js:165-330; INSERT organization_users at :316) and atomicAcceptInvitation (:364+; INSERT at :422) write no audit row in their transaction. The invite is audited only after commit, best-effort, via auditService.logAction (server/services/tenant/invitation-delivery.ts:120-139), and the acceptance that creates the membership is not audited at all. (d) Cache invalidation is per instance; other instances converge within the 60s TTL (server/middleware/orgMembership.ts:26-28, :45).
records.fixedBy: 8167aef12 (P1-41: role change and removal audited with a reason); c1f2cb9ca (a role change revokes the cached membership); ddc8c0db5 (re-role and remove with a reason from the admin surface); code at server/services/tenant/membership-change.ts:49-158 and server/routes/tenant-users.ts:575-692
records.remaining: Platform suspension is audited under tenant 0, after commit and best-effort. There is no tenant-administrator suspend action. Granting access (member creation and invitation acceptance) writes no chained audit row in its transaction. Cross-instance cache revocation waits up to 60s.
records.severityRationale: Role changes and removals now leave a chained, same-transaction record with old and new role, reason and actor. That is the evidence an access review and Annex 11 §12 need, so the original P1 impact is closed for the pilot. In a sales-led, founder-supported pilot, suspension is a platform-operator act and membership grants are partly recorded (the invite row carries the role), so the remaining gaps belong before enterprise GA.
records.humanTestingNote: A tenant admin can re-role or remove a member, with a required reason, but cannot suspend one. A platform suspension does not appear in the organisation's audit trail or its Administrative changes report. Workaround: remove the member (audited) instead of suspending.
records.instructions:
1. server/routes/admin/master-admin.ts:408-460 (PATCH /users/:id/status): run SELECT status ... FOR UPDATE, the UPDATE users and the audit inside one transaction(async client => ...) (server/db/runtime.ts). Write writeChainedAuditRow(client, ...) for tenant 0, plus one chained row per organisation the user belongs to (SELECT organization_id FROM organization_users WHERE user_id = $1), each inside that organisation's verified scope (inVerifiedOrgScope / runWithTenantScope) so RLS admits it. Use action 'member_suspended' / 'member_reinstated' with details {from, to, reason, actorScope:'platform'}. An audit failure rolls the change back and returns 500. After commit, call invalidateOrgMembershipCache(id). Add the two action constants to server/services/tenant/membership-change.ts and to the action lists in server/services/audit/compliance-reports/queries/administrative-changes.ts and access-review.ts.
2. server/services/atomicQuotaService.js: in atomicCreateUser (:165-330) and atomicAcceptInvitation (:364-440), before COMMIT, write a chained row on the same client: action 'member_added', resourceType 'organization_users', resourceId the user id, details {targetUserId, previousRole:null, newRole, via:'direct_invite'|'invitation_accept', invitationId?, invitedBy?}. Import writeChainedAuditRow the way the file's other server imports are resolved. An audit failure rolls the membership back.
3. Founder decision: does the pilot need a tenant-level suspend? Removal already revokes access with an audit row. If yes: add suspended_at TIMESTAMPTZ, suspended_by INTEGER and suspension_reason TEXT to organization_users in a NEW additive migration (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS), inserted in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES before the final tenant-sweep pair (ci:migration-set-order). Treat a suspended membership as non-member in the server/middleware/orgMembership.ts lookup (fail closed, 403). Add suspendMember/reinstateMember to membership-change.ts with an in-transaction chained row. Add PATCH /api/tenant-users/:organizationId/:userId/status {status, reason}, with requireAdmin, the self-change refusal and the last-administrator guard. Add a Suspend action to client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/AdminMemberActions.tsx.
4. Tests: extend the server/routes/__tests__/tenant-users-audit.test.ts pattern to the new paths, and add cases to tests/db/admin-change-audit.dbtest.ts. A platform suspend appears on the member's organisation chain and in the Administrative changes report, and a forced writeChainedAuditRow failure leaves users.status unchanged. Show each new test red on HEAD before the change.
Commit directly on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0).
records.acceptance: (a) A platform suspend or reactivate writes exactly one chained audit_logs row in each organisation the user belongs to (plus tenant 0), in the same transaction, with from, to, reason and actor. With writeChainedAuditRow forced to throw, the route returns 500 and users.status is unchanged. Fails on HEAD. (b) Creating a member and accepting an invitation each write one chained 'member_added' row before COMMIT, and a forced audit failure leaves no organization_users row. Fails on HEAD. (c) The rows appear in the organisation's signed audit export and in the Administrative changes and Access review reports. (d) If tenant suspend is adopted, the suspended member's next request on the same instance returns 403.
records.dependencies: none (founder decision only for the optional tenant-level suspend)

records.title: Gateway transmit now checks signing authority and refuses authorship and the package creator, but still records the signature after the bytes leave; two transmit paths remain
records.evidenceAtHead: OPEN: In server/services/submission-gateways/governed-transmit.ts, executeGovernedTransmit calls gw.transmit at :662 and only afterwards (:736-857) opens the transaction that writes recordGovernedAction and persistGovernedActionSignature. If that transaction fails, it sets ledgerWriteFailed = true (:852) and returns success. Ran `npx vitest run server/services/submission-gateways/__tests__/governed-transmit-signature.test.ts`: 12/12 pass, including :159 'rolls the ledger transaction back and reports ledgerWriteFailed when the signature row cannot be written'. That test confirms the transmit completes with no signature on record. The route only reports the gap in the HTTP response (server/routes/mdx-submission-gateway.ts:331-363, transmitOutcomeNotices); nothing durable flags the transmittal. MEANING: SIGN_MEANINGS is still ['authorship','review','approval','responsibility','release'] (mdx-submission-gateway.ts:82, accepted at :274). 'authorship' is now refused server-side (server/services/submission-gateways/governed-transmit-checks.ts:248-262 via requiresIndependence) and removed from the form (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/GatewayTransmittals.tsx:271-279, default 'release'), but 'review', 'approval' and 'responsibility' are still accepted for a transmission. TWO PATHS: both are reachable under 'Submit & file' (client/src/concept2cure/v2/registryModel.ts:638, :670). (a) POST /api/submissions/sequences/:seqId/transmit (server/routes/submissions.ts:1887; client SubmissionCenter.tsx:856) requires a committed governed signature with intent 'transmit' BEFORE the gateway (server/services/submission-service/submission-service.ts:2100-2107) and voids it on a pre-wire refusal (:2052-2066). (b) POST /api/mdx/gateways/:region/:gateway/transmit (mdx-submission-gateway.ts:278; client GatewayTransmittals.tsx:482) and the AnA command (server/services/ana-ri/mdx-command-handlers.ts:821-860) go through executeGovernedTransmit, which signs after transmit. CLOSED SINCE AUDIT: checkSigningAuthority now runs before re-auth (mdx-submission-gateway.ts:297-301; governed-transmit-checks.ts:217), the package creator is refused (SIGNER_IS_AUTHOR), and so is the authorship meaning.
records.fixedBy: e7fdd5c39 (SEC-1008-1: only a role that may sign transmits; authority checked before re-auth); f7973d225 (package creator cannot transmit; 'authorship' refused, governed-transmit-checks.ts:248-283)
records.remaining: (1) On the package-model gateway path (HTTP route and AnA command), the signature is still written after the irreversible send, and a failed write is tolerated. (2) The transmit meaning is not fixed to 'release'; 'review' is accepted. (3) Two transmit paths with different signing ceremonies remain reachable.
records.severityRationale: The pilot's core regulatory act is an FDA ESG transmission. On a path reachable from the launch navigation, a submission can still reach FDA with no Part 11 signature on record, and a test executed at HEAD proves it. The window is narrow (a database failure between the gateway call and the signature commit), but the ordering defect is exactly what a sponsor's QA audit flags under §11.10(f)/§11.70. Pilot users must not rely on it for production filings until the signature commits first.
records.humanTestingNote: Not visible unless the database fails between the gateway call and the signature write. Testers will see two transmit surfaces with different ceremonies: Submission Center > Dispatch, which signs first, and Gateway transmittals, which signs at transmit. On the second, a transmission can be signed as 'Review'. Use the Submission Center sequence path for test transmissions.
records.instructions:
1. server/services/submission-gateways/governed-transmit.ts: move the signature transaction BEFORE gw.transmit (:662). After assertTransmitterIndependent (:658), take pool.connect(), BEGIN, then recordGovernedAction(command 'sign', target as at :743, payload {meaning, region, gateway, bundleSha256, sequence, submissionType, contentFingerprint {assembled, atTransmit}, intent:'transmit'}), then persistGovernedActionSignature with binding {digest: bundle.sha256, basis: BINDING_BASIS.TRANSMITTED_BUNDLE_SHA256}, then COMMIT. On any failure, ROLLBACK and throw GovernedTransmitInternalError('transmit-signature-before-wire', err). The gateway is never called.
2. Wrap gw.transmit in try/catch. If refusedBeforeWire(err) (server/services/submission-gateways/index.ts:152), void the signature in its own transaction with voidSignatureForRefusedAct (server/services/part11/signature-persistence.ts:253), mirroring voidingSignatureOnRefusal (server/services/submission-service/submission-service.ts:1069), and rethrow. Otherwise keep the signature (the bytes may be at the agency) and rethrow.
3. After a successful transmit, write a receipt in a second transaction: a chained row (recordGovernedAction command 'transmit-receipt' or writeChainedAuditRow) naming signatureId, transmittalId, transmissionId, contentAfterTransmit, the filed-sequence facts and the pre-transmit findings, plus the existing UPDATE submission_transmittals metadata stamp (:832-845). If that fails, return receiptWriteFailed (replacing ledgerWriteFailed; the signature already exists) and surface it through transmitOutcomeNotices.
4. Meaning: in server/routes/mdx-submission-gateway.ts transmitBody (:273-274), replace z.enum(SIGN_MEANINGS) with z.literal('release').default('release'), and keep SIGN_MEANINGS for the technical-rejection body (:526). In executeGovernedTransmit, refuse any other meaning with GovernedTransmitRefusal 422. In client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/GatewayTransmittals.tsx:271-279, replace the select with a fixed 'Release: I authorize submission to the agency' statement. In server/services/ana-ri/mdx-command-handlers.ts (~:837), pass 'release'.
5. Tests: in server/services/submission-gateways/__tests__/governed-transmit-signature.test.ts, invert :159 so that with failSignature, executeGovernedTransmit rejects and the gateway transmit mock is called 0 times (red on HEAD). Add a test that a pre-wire gateway refusal voids the signature, and one that a receipt-write failure leaves the signature committed and reports receiptWriteFailed. Update the AnA handler tests (server/services/ana-ri/__tests__) that assert the old ordering.
6. Founder decision, then apply CLAUDE.md's deletion rule: is package-model transmit (Gateway transmittals) in the pilot? If not, return 410 from POST /api/mdx/gateways/:region/:gateway/transmit naming the replacement, POST /api/submissions/sequences/:seqId/transmit (client SubmissionCenter.tsx:856), and remove only the transmit form from GatewayTransmittals.tsx (keep list, status, ack and technical-rejection). Name the replacement file and its reachability test in the commit message. If both paths stay, steps 1-5 make their ordering equivalent.
Commit directly on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0).
records.acceptance: (a) With persistGovernedActionSignature forced to throw, executeGovernedTransmit rejects with transmit-signature-before-wire and the gateway transmit mock is called 0 times. On HEAD it is called once and ledgerWriteFailed is true (red first). (b) A gateway refusal before the wire leaves the electronic_signatures row voided and no transmittal row. (c) POST /api/mdx/gateways/fda/esg/transmit with meaning 'review' returns 422, and the form offers no meaning choice. (d) Either exactly one transmit route remains, with the other returning 410 and naming its replacement, or the founder's decision to keep both is recorded and both sign before the wire.
records.dependencies: P11-01 (signing authority; already enforced on this path by e7fdd5c39); founder decision for step 6 (one transmit path).

records.title: Validation pack still not run in CI or bound to a release; no release tags, versions or per-release change records
records.evidenceAtHead: (1) No workflow in .github/workflows runs validation:iq or validation:oq (package.json:70-71; grep for run-iq / run-all.mjs / validation:iq / validation:oq finds nothing). ci.yml:428-432 runs only ci:validation-traceability, which checks that URS citations resolve, and it already did so at 92ccdba1 (ci.yml:397). (2) The release-evidence gate (ci.yml:2559-2609 -> .github/workflows/release-evidence.yml) packages CI job conclusions and npm-audit, not IQ/OQ results. (3) Harness defaults in tests/validation/lib/harness.mjs:52-58: RUN_DATE is now resolveRunDate(), today's date validated (scripts/validation/env-files.mjs:46-54); it was hard-coded '2026-09-27' at 92ccdba1. TEST_USER_EMAIL still defaults to the founder's address, CHROMIUM_PATH to /opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/..., and EVIDENCE_ROOT into the repo (docs/evidence/W3/<date>); scripts/validation/run-iq.mjs:24-26 has the same defaults. (4) `git tag | wc -l` -> 0. `git ls-remote --tags origin` shows only v1.0.0, a GitHub tag object dated 2026-02-12 that points at 8d56db74, a commit absent from concept2cure-v2 history. (5) .husky/pre-push:26-70 refuses any push whose remote ref is not refs/heads/concept2cure-v2, including refs/tags/v*. The only bypass is ALLOW_NON_CANONICAL_PUSH=1, yet .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:17-19 deploys on v* tag pushes. (6) GET /api/version returns only {commit, startedAt} (server/startup/inline-endpoints.ts:196-198). (7) CHANGELOG.md has only an [Unreleased] section; no per-release change record (change, impact, testing, approval) exists.
records.remaining: Everything material. IQ/OQ/traceability is not executed against a deployed environment by any workflow. No validated release version is produced, tagged or published with its validation pack, and nothing records per-release change control. The harness still defaults to the founder's identity and a machine-specific Chromium path, and writes evidence into the repo. /api/version names no release. The pre-push hook blocks pushing release tags. Only the run date was parameterised.
records.severityRationale: A GxP design partner has to validate its intended use and audit the supplier before relying on the system in production. They will ask which validated version they are running and for the change and regression evidence of each release. At HEAD neither can be answered: there is no version, no tag, no per-release IQ/OQ run and no change record. This does not stop the pilot from starting under founder support, so it is not P0. It must exist before pilot users rely on the system for GxP records.
records.humanTestingNote: Not observable in the UI. There is no release number, so testers should record the commit from GET /api/version in every defect report.
records.instructions:
1. Founder decisions, recorded in docs/RELEASE_GOVERNANCE.md: the version scheme (vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH), who approves a release, and how release tags are created. Recommended: tags are created by a CI workflow through the GitHub API, not by a local push, so .husky/pre-push (Rule 0 enforcement) stays unchanged.
2. Add .github/workflows/release-cut.yml (workflow_dispatch, input version). (a) Refuse unless github.sha is on concept2cure-v2 and the CI verdict for that SHA is success; reuse the ci-verdict job logic from deploy-aws.yml. (b) Refuse unless docs/releases/<version>.md exists with Change, Impact, Testing and Approval sections and a named approver. records.acceptance: (a) release-cut on a SHA with a forced OQ failure fails and creates no tag or release (shown first). On a green SHA it produces tag vX.Y.Z and a GitHub Release carrying validation-pack-vX.Y.Z (IQ, OQ and traceability results naming the base URL and commit) and docs/releases/vX.Y.Z.md. (b) With CI=true and VALIDATION_USER_EMAIL unset, the harness exits non-zero before any request (selftest red on HEAD). (c) GET /api/version on the deployed environment returns {version:'vX.Y.Z', commit:<sha>}. (d) release-cut refuses when the change record is missing or has no approver.
records.dependencies: A reachable staging environment with seeded validation credentials (launch infra rows); founder decisions on version scheme, release approver and tag creation.
